description: Driven participant looking to showcase skills and design on NASA Frontier Development and Research
summary:
OHTLI is a visionOS app that turns NASA Mars data into a spatial planning table for a Marswalk. Astronauts start at a 3D Mars globe layered with Viking color, MOLA elevation, THEMIS day/night infrared and USGS geology, then drop into a Gale Crater sector built from a real MRO HiRISE 1 m terrain model. A deterministic Weighted A* planner reads slope and distance from that terrain, rejects unsafe grades, and draws a modeled safe route next to the naive straight line, with a walk-back reserve for oxygen, CO₂ and cooling water.

Simulated EVA crew markers show suit vitals: oxygen, metabolic load, cooling water, walk-back margin, dose and radio status. A simulated dust event freezes the crew and computes a one-way return to the habitat airlock. The same mission can then be flown from a drone view or walked at helmet height.

Existing tools like Mars Trek are regional and flat. OHTLI targets the hyperlocal, safety-first decisions of a single EVA, in the same 3D space where the crew plans together. All crew readings and hazards are clearly labeled as simulated.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

OHTLI is a spatial computing planner for a human Marswalk. It runs in one movable volume that moves through four stages:

1. Mars Globe: interactive 3D Mars with switchable NASA layers (Viking optical, MOLA elevation, THEMIS day and night infrared, USGS geologic map SIM 3292) and pins for Gale/Mount Sharp, the Altadena boxwork target and Jezero.

2. Tabletop: a Gale Crater sector from the MRO HiRISE stereo DTM DTEEC_040770_1755_039280_1755_U01 and its registered orthophoto, with optical and DTM-derived slope layers. The airlock and destination can be moved and the route recalculates.

3. Drone view: an immersive aerial flight over the same terrain and route.

4. Helmet view: ground level at 1.8 m eye height on the native ~1 m HiRISE grid, so the crew can preview what the terrain looks like before leaving the airlock.

HOW IT WORKS

- Routing: a deterministic Weighted A* search over an ~8 m grid derived from the HiRISE DTM. Hard gates reject slopes above the walking limit; edge costs combine distance, grade and modeled exertion. The planner compares the routed path to a straight line and reports distance, time and a walk-back reserve across oxygen, CO₂ and cooling water (water from modeled energy at 2,480 kJ/kg), including a 30-minute science stop.

- Crew and emergency: simulated EVA crew carry vitals (O₂, metabolic W, cooling water, walk-back margin, dose, radio line of sight, terrain class). The emergency demo freezes a crew member during simulated dust and plans a one-way return to Airlock Alpha, showing the limiting resource.

- Explanation: an optional on-device Apple Intelligence (Foundation Models) summary explains the return using only the planner's numbers. It never computes safety values itself, and an offline scripted fallback is always available.

- Collaboration: SharePlay group-activity support so several crew can review the same plan.

WHY IT MATTERS

NASA's first priority is crew safety. Mars Trek and USGS maps are regional and global; a single EVA needs hyperlocal answers: can we get there, which way, and can we get back? With a 4–24 minute signal delay, crews must plan for themselves. OHTLI puts that answer on a shared 3D table at human scale.

TOOLS

Swift, SwiftUI, RealityKit, visionOS 27 (Apple Vision Pro / Simulator), GroupActivities (SharePlay), Foundation Models, Swift Testing/XCTest, Python data-prep scripts (GDAL-style resampling of PDS and USGS COG products), Blender + usdzip for the habitat scene. Fully offline: all terrain and globe layers are bundled.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN FACTORS

- Spatial-first UI following Apple's visionOS HIG: look-and-pinch, no head-locked clutter, controls attached to the movable volume, scene moves instead of the user's camera to avoid motion sickness.

- Honesty about data: every measured product is cited in-app and in the repo; Airlock Alpha, crew telemetry, dust and suit capacities are labeled SIMULATED or ASSUMPTION. The synthetic horizon skirt and sky are marked as illustrative and do not extend the measured HiRISE footprint.

- Inspired by the Curiosity boxwork campaign at Mount Sharp (the 2025 "Altadena" drill target) named in the challenge text. The crop's exact overlap with Altadena is not verified and is labeled as such.

LIMITATIONS

Prototype only, not validated EVA guidance. No live telemetry or live Mars weather. Suit capacities and thresholds are demonstration inputs. A bounded search cannot prove that no route exists.
